pr_title: distsql: control the sending rate of copIteratorTaskSender if keepOrder is true
pr_body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to TiDB! Please read TiDB's [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document **BEFORE** filing this PR.
-->

### What problem does this PR solve? <!--add issue link with summary if exists-->

Closes #11468 

### What is changed and how it works?

- Introduce `sendRate` to control the number of inflight tasks within concurrency * 2.

If `keepOrder` is true, we must control the sending rate to prevent all tasks being done (aka. all of the responses are buffered) by `copIteratorWorker`. We keep the number of inflight tasks within the number of `concurrency * 2`. It sends one more task if a task has been finished in `copIterator.Next`.

review_comments: Can we return an error instead of panic?

It's an `unreachable` path and we should panic here.
An example: https://github.com/golang/go/blob/master/src/bufio/bufio.go#L395-L396
Why can't we return an error for an unreachable path?
Let's discuss in the thread below.
Is this an individual bug-fix?
A tiny adjustment.

I do not really understand, if a region is split, two new tasks will be constructed.
Where will the block happen?
Task B will be blocked when Task A is sent into `respChan` but the client hasn't received Task A.
It's better to return an error instead of just panic.

It's an `unreachable` path and we should panic here.
An example: https://github.com/golang/go/blob/master/src/bufio/bufio.go#L395-L396

It's unreachable only when programmer writes code correctly. But everyone makes mistake. It's better to return an error to make our user notice that we have made a mistake. And that mistake should not impact the long running database service.

There are several cons using error but not panic:
1. `rateLimit.putToken` is dirty with an unmeaning error return value.
2. The user of `rateLimit.putToken` has to do a redundant error check.
3. Make a bug hard and late to reveal.

Besides, we should consider using `recover` to handle mistakes made by programmers.

You can see many cases with `panic("unreachable")` in go world and every mistake make by programmers may panic and let bugs revealed.

https://github.com/golang/go/search?q=panic%28%22unreachable%22%29&unscoped_q=panic%28%22unreachable%22%29

> 1. rateLimit.putToken is dirty with an unmeaning error return value.
> 2. The user of rateLimit.putToken has to do a redundant error check.
> 3. Make a bug hard and late to reveal.

IMHO,
Golang is a tool that the programmers will use, while TiDB is a tool that the customers will use.
These 3 points are all from the perspective of a programmer, but not from the perspective of a customer.
We need to make the behavior be more acceptable to the customers.
Agreed with @XuHuaiyu. That's why we changed most of the panic in our codebase to error in the past few PRs.

For customers, we should use `defer` to handle this sort of panic.
like https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/730e140/server/conn.go#L1258-L1276
`recover()` on that goroutine doesn't work. If you are going to use the `panic-recover` mechanism, you should `recover` in the gogoutine where the function caller belongs to.
Otherwise, in this circumstance, if a token cannot be put into the channel, it may lead to unexpected behavior, I do not think the caller could handle the expectation correctly.

> `recover()` on that goroutine doesn't work. If you are going to use the `panic-recover` mechanism, you should `recover` in the gogoutine where the function caller belongs to.

Yes, it's recovered by https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/730e1408cfbf75ed3c45fd98e3a8bdcf5b15d89a/server/conn.go#L1258-L1276 with `streamResult` and  https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/730e1408cfbf75ed3c45fd98e3a8bdcf5b15d89a/distsql/select_result.go#L90-L102 with `selectResult`.
okay.

`copIterator.Next()` may not be always called, for example:

cop.Next, cop.Next, cop.Close ... 

So it's better to move the `putToken` to the worker when it finished its task.

It's better to remove the `done` channel, don't mixture the logic with pure library code.
`rateLimit` should just focus on one thing: token
